definition: Start from a place where the meaning is sound. If the word begins with همزة الوصل (ٱ), give it a vowel; when you join it to the word before, it is not said at all.
list: A verb whose third letter has an original ضمة: ضمة
Verbs whose third letter has a ضمة that is not original: كسرة
The nouns ٱبْن، ٱبْنَت، ٱمْرُؤ، ٱمْرَأَة، ٱثْنَان، ٱثْنَتَان، ٱسْم: كسرة

facts.q: You start at ٱلْحَمْدُ. The همزة الوصل takes…
facts.why: With ال it is always فتحة.

facts.q: You start at ٱهْدِنَا. The همزة الوصل takes…
facts.why: The third letter (د) has a كسرة, so the همزة takes كسرة.

facts.q: You start at ٱدْعُ. The همزة الوصل takes…
facts.why: The third letter (ع) has an original ضمة.

facts.q: You start at ٱمْشُوا۟ (38:6). The همزة الوصل takes…
facts.why: The ضمة on ش is not original. Its root form is ٱمْشِيُوا; the ضمة was added, so the همزة takes كسرة.

facts.q: You start at ٱبْنَ. The همزة الوصل takes…
facts.why: It is one of the nouns that always take كسرة.

facts.q: What happens to همزة الوصل when you join it to the word before?
options: It is not said at all
It is always said with فتحة
facts.why: It is only said when you start with it.

facts.q: Where should you start again after a stop?
facts.why: A bad start can change the meaning.

The third letter (ع) has an original ضمة: start with a ضمة, اُدْعُ.

Inside the word the ٱ is never said: read بِسْمِ. (Starting on ٱسْم alone, it would be اِسْم.)

en: The open space: the madd letters
definition: الجوف is the empty space of the throat and mouth. It is the مخرج of the three حروف المد: ا after فتحة, وْ after ضمة, يْ after كسرة. They end with the breath and have no fixed point, so they are also called الحروف الهوائية.
letters: ا و ي (حروف المد)
tip: To find any letter's مخرج, put a همزة with a vowel before it and give it a سكون or شدة: أَبْ، أَتْ، أَثْ. Where the sound stops is its مخرج.
list: 17 in the view of الخليل and ابن الجزري, which most teachers follow. سيبويه counts 16 (no الجوف) and الفراء 14.

facts.q: Which letters come from الجوف?
options: ا، وْ، يْ as حروف مد
facts.why: الجوف is the مخرج of the three حروف المد only.

facts.q: Which وْ comes from الجوف?
options: The وْ after a ضمة, as in يَقُولُ
The وْ after a فتحة, as in خَوْفٍ
A وَ with a فتحة, as in وَلَدٌ
facts.why: Only a و ساكنة after a ضمة is a حرف مد. After a فتحة it is لين.

facts.q: In قِيلَ, the ي is…
facts.why: A ي ساكنة after a كسرة is a حرف مد.

facts.q: Why are the حروف المد called هوائية?
options: Their sound ends with the breath
facts.why: They have no fixed point to stop on. Their sound runs out with the air of the mouth and throat.

facts.q: In بَيْتِ, where does the ي come from?
facts.why: It is لين, not مد. Only حروف المد come from الجوف; a لين ي comes from the place of the ي.

facts.q: How many مخارج are there in the view most teachers follow (ابن الجزري)?
facts.why: ابن الجزري follows الخليل: 17. سيبويه counts 16 and الفراء 14.

examples.note: ا after a فتحة, وْ after a ضمة: two حروف المد from الجوف; the sound runs on the breath, touching nothing.
وْ after a ضمة is a حرف مد: its sound comes from الجوف and ends when the breath ends.
يْ after a كسرة is a حرف مد from الجوف, held two counts with no fixed point.
The ا after the فتحة on ك: the mouth is open and nothing meets; that is الجوف.
وْ after the ضمة on ق: a حرف مد from الجوف; the word has a second one before ن.
يْ after a كسرة, then ا after a فتحة: two حروف المد in one word.

definition: The throat has three مخارج, two letters each: أقصى الحلق (deepest, next to the chest) ء هـ; وسط الحلق ع ح; أدنى الحلق (nearest the mouth) غ خ.
letters: ء هـ · ع ح · غ خ
tip: Drill the pairs learners mix up: ح with هـ, and ع with ء.

facts.q: Which letters come from أقصى الحلق (the deepest point)?
facts.why: أقصى الحلق is the deepest point: ء then هـ.

facts.q: Which letters come from وسط الحلق?
facts.why: The middle of the throat gives ع and ح.

facts.q: Which letters come from أدنى الحلق (nearest the mouth)?
facts.why: The top of the throat, next to the mouth, gives غ and خ.

facts.q: How many مخارج are in the throat?
facts.why: Three points, two letters each.

facts.q: ح and هـ differ in that…
options: ح: وسط الحلق; هـ: أقصى الحلق
facts.why: They are often mixed up, but their points differ.

facts.q: The six throat letters are also the letters of which rule?
facts.why: A نون ساكنة or تنوين before a throat letter is said clearly.

facts.q: Which word starts with a letter from أدنى الحلق?
facts.why: خ is from أدنى الحلق; ح and ع from the middle, ء from the deepest point.

examples.note: The أ from the deepest part of the throat, then حْ from its middle (وسط الحلق).
خْ from the nearest part of the throat to the mouth (أدنى الحلق).
أ then هْ: both from the deepest part of the throat (أقصى الحلق).
عْ from the middle of the throat, the same place as ح.
غْ from أدنى الحلق, the same place as خ.
أْ: a همزة with سكون, said fully from the deepest part of the throat.

en: Back of the tongue: ق ك
definition: ق comes from the back of the tongue (أقصى اللسان), near the throat, against the palate above it. ك comes from just below it, a little nearer the mouth. They are called اللهويتان, after the uvula (اللهاة).
letters: ق ك

facts.q: Where does ق come from?
options: The deepest point of the throat
facts.why: Near the throat, with the palate above it. ق is the first مخرج of the tongue, at its back.

facts.q: Compared with ق, ك comes from…
options: a point a little nearer the mouth
a point deeper toward the throat
facts.why: ك is just below ق, toward the mouth.

facts.q: ق and ك are called…
facts.why: They are named after اللهاة (the uvula) near their مخرج.

facts.q: Besides the مخرج, what makes ق sound different from ك?
options: ك has قلقلة and ق does not
ق is heavy and has قلقلة
ك is heavy and ق is light
facts.why: ق is مستعلٍ and مجهور; ك is light and مهموس. ق: جهر، شدة، استعلاء، قلقلة. ك: همس، شدة، استفال.

facts.q: How many مخارج are on أقصى اللسان?
facts.why: ق and ك each have their own point.

facts.q: Which pair is easy to confuse because their مخارج are neighbours?
facts.why: Their points sit next to each other at the back of the tongue.

examples.note: قْ: the back of the tongue, next to the throat, against the palate above it.
كّ: a little lower than ق and nearer the mouth, against the palate.
كْ with سكون: the back of the tongue meets the palate just in front of the place of ق.
قُ then كُ side by side: the tongue moves a little forward from ق to ك.
ق with a فتحة: still from أقصى اللسان, and heavy.
After لْ, the back of the tongue closes on the palate for كُ.
قْ in the first word revealed: the back of the tongue, then the قلقلة.

en: Middle and edges of the tongue: ج ش ي ض ل
definition: ج ش ي (the ي that is not a حرف مد) come from the middle of the tongue against the palate above it. ض comes from one or both edges of the tongue against the upper molars; the left side is easier and more common. ل comes from the front part of the edge, up to the tip, against the gums of the upper front teeth.
letters: ج ش ي · ض · ل

facts.q: ج ش ي come from…
facts.why: With the palate above it. They share one مخرج: وسط اللسان.

facts.q: Which ي comes from وسط اللسان?
facts.why: As in يَوْمٍ and بَيْتِ. A ي that is a حرف مد comes from الجوف.

facts.q: ض comes from…
options: one or both edges of the tongue against the upper molars
the tip of the tongue with the upper front teeth
facts.why: ض is the only letter from حافة اللسان with the molars.

facts.q: For ض, which side of the tongue is easier and more common?
facts.why: Both sides are correct; the left is easier, and both together are the least common.

facts.q: ل comes from…
options: the front edge of the tongue
facts.why: Up to its tip, against the gums of the upper teeth. ل uses the edge of the tongue from near the front to the tip.

facts.q: ض and ظ differ in their مخرج: …
options: both: the edge of the tongue
ض: the edge; ظ: the tip
both: the tip of the tongue
facts.why: ض is from the edge of the tongue with the molars; ظ is from the tip with the edges of the upper front teeth. Mixing them changes the word, so learn each one's place.

examples.note: يّ is not a حرف مد: it comes from the middle of the tongue against the palate above it.
جْ: the middle of the tongue against the palate, the place shared with ش and ي.
شْ: from the middle of the tongue and the palate, like ج and ي.
يَ with a فتحة is not a حرف مد: it comes from وسط اللسان.
ض: the edge of the tongue against the upper molars; the left side is easier and more common.
لْ: the front of the tongue's edge up to its tip, against the gums of the upper front teeth.
ض from the edge of the tongue, then a light ل from the front of the edge.

definition: ن: the tip of the tongue against the gum of the upper front teeth, a little below ل. ر: close to ن but further onto the top of the tongue. ط د ت: the tip against the roots of the upper front teeth. ص س ز: the tip of the tongue, near the lower front teeth, with a narrow gap for the whistle. ظ ذ ث: the tip against the edges of the upper front teeth.
letters: ن · ر · ط د ت · ص س ز · ظ ذ ث
tip: Drill the pairs learners mix up: ط ت · ص س · ذ ز ظ · ث س.

facts.q: ط د ت come from…
options: the tip near the lower front teeth
the tip against the upper teeth's roots
the tip against the upper teeth's edges
facts.why: They share one مخرج; they differ in their صفات.

facts.q: ظ ذ ث come from…
options: the tip against the upper teeth's edges
the tip against the upper teeth's roots
the tip near the lower front teeth
facts.why: The tip just touches the edges of the upper front teeth.

facts.q: ص س ز come from…
options: the tip near the lower front teeth
the tip against the upper teeth's roots
the tip against the upper teeth's edges
facts.why: With a narrow gap. The narrow gap gives their whistle (الصفير).

facts.q: ر compared with ن:
options: they are exactly the same point
ر is a little further back
facts.why: ر is a little further onto the top of the tongue. They are neighbours at the tip of the tongue.

facts.q: ذ and ز differ in their مخرج: …
options: ذ: upper teeth; ز: lower teeth
facts.why: ذ: the tip with the edges of the upper teeth; ز: the tip near the lower front teeth. Learners often say ز for ذ; keep the tip on the upper teeth.

facts.q: Which group are called النطعية?
facts.why: They come from near نِطع (the front of the palate).

examples.note: دّ: the tip against the roots of the upper front teeth; نْ: the tip against their gum.
سْ: the tip near the lower front teeth, with a narrow gap for the whistle.
ذّ: the tip of the tongue against the edges of the upper front teeth, like ظ and ث.
رْ: close to the place of ن, but further onto the top of the tongue.
صْ: the place of س and ز, the tip near the lower front teeth.
دّ: the tip on the roots of the upper front teeth, where ت and ط are made too.
ث: the tip of the tongue against the edges of the upper front teeth.
طِ: the tip of the tongue against the roots of the upper front teeth, with د and ت.
تَ: the tip on the roots of the upper front teeth, the place of ط and د.
ز: a whistle letter, from the tip near the lower front teeth, with س and ص.

definition: ف: the inside of the lower lip against the edges of the upper front teeth. و ب م (the و that is not a حرف مد): both lips; ب and م close them, و rounds them without closing. الخيشوم, the nasal passage, is the مخرج of the غنة of ن and م.
letters: ف · و ب م · الغنة

facts.q: ف comes from…
facts.why: The inside of the lower lip with the edges of the upper front teeth. ف is the only letter from this مخرج.

facts.q: ب م و (not a حرف مد) come from…
options: the lower lip and the upper teeth
facts.why: They share the lips.

facts.q: How do ب، م and و differ?
options: all three leave the lips open
و closes the lips more than ب
و rounds the lips, not closing
facts.why: ب and م close the lips. The و is made with rounded, open lips.

facts.q: الخيشوم is the مخرج of…
facts.why: The غنة of ن and م comes from the nasal passage.

facts.q: How many مخارج do the lips have?
facts.why: ف has its own point; و ب م share the other.

facts.q: If you pinch your nose while saying نّ, the sound stops. What does that show?
options: The غنة comes from the throat
facts.why: Blocking the nasal passage blocks the غنة.

facts.q: Why be careful with a مْ before و or ف?
options: The ميم can slip into them
facts.why: They are close to the ميم. تحفة الأطفال: «وَاحْذَرْ لَدَى وَاوٍ وَفَا أَنْ تَخْتَفِي».

فّ: the inside of the lower lip against the edges of the upper front teeth.
The first وُ: both lips round without closing. The second is a حرف مد from الجوف.
بْ: both lips close firmly, then open with a قلقلة.
مّ: the lips stay closed while the غنة, two counts, comes from الخيشوم.
مْ: the lips close for م, then open for ع.
فْ with سكون: the lower lip rests on the edges of the upper front teeth.

definition: الهمس: the breath flows with the letter. Its 10 letters gather in «فَحَثَّهُ شَخْصٌ سَكَتْ». الجهر, its opposite: the breath is held back. Every other letter is مجهور.
letters: الهمس: ف ح ث ه ش خ ص س ك ت

facts.q: Which phrase gathers the letters of الهمس?
facts.why: These are the 10 مهموس letters.

facts.q: What is الهمس?
options: The tongue rises to the palate
The breath flows with the letter
facts.why: Its opposite, الجهر, holds the breath back.

facts.q: How many letters are مهموس?
facts.why: ف ح ث ه ش خ ص س ك ت.

facts.q: Which of these letters is مجهور?
facts.why: د is not in فَحَثَّهُ شَخْصٌ سَكَتْ.

facts.q: س and ز come from the same مخرج. What separates them?
options: ز is heavy and س is light
س is مهموس, ز is مجهور
س has قلقلة and ز does not
facts.why: They differ only in الهمس and الجهر.

facts.q: What is the opposite of الهمس?
facts.why: Each of these two-sided qualities has an opposite.

examples.note: خْ, سِ, فَ: three مهموسة letters in a row; hear the breath run on with the خْ.
حْ: the breath flows on with the letter; that is الهمس.
سْ then تَ, both مهموسة: the breath runs through the سْ.
At the stop, تْ ends with a light breath: it is مهموسة as well as شديدة.
هْ then كَ, both مهموسة: the breath runs with each; say the هْ clearly.
زْ: the place of س, but the breath is held back: مجهورة, the opposite of الهمس.
ثْ: the breath flows between the tongue and the upper teeth.
صْ: heavy, but still مهموسة; the breath runs with it.
شْ: the breath runs and spreads with it.

definition: الشدة: the sound is held back completely when the letter has a سكون. Its 8 letters gather in «أَجِدْ قَطٍ بَكَتْ». التوسط (البينية): the sound is partly held. Its 5 letters gather in «لِنْ عُمَرْ». الرخاوة: the sound flows; it covers all the other letters.
letters: الشدة: أ ج د ق ط ب ك ت · التوسط: ل ن ع م ر

facts.q: Which phrase gathers the letters of الشدة?
facts.why: These 8 letters stop the sound.

facts.q: Which phrase gathers the letters of التوسط?
facts.why: These 5 letters are between شدة and رخاوة.

facts.q: What happens to the sound in الشدة?
facts.why: With a سكون. Example: أَجْ، أَدْ.

facts.q: Which of these letters is رخو?
facts.why: س is in neither أَجِدْ قَطٍ بَكَتْ nor لِنْ عُمَرْ.

facts.q: Which two letters are both شديد and مهموس?
facts.why: They are in both أَجِدْ قَطٍ بَكَتْ and فَحَثَّهُ شَخْصٌ سَكَتْ: the sound stops, then a little breath follows.

facts.q: ع belongs to…
facts.why: ع is in لِنْ عُمَرْ.

facts.q: How many letters have الشدة?
facts.why: أ ج د ق ط ب ك ت.

examples.note: دْ: the sound is held back completely at its مخرج (الشدة), then it bounces out (قلقلة).
عْ lets part of the sound run (التوسط); دْ holds it all back (الشدة).
حْ: the sound runs on freely (الرخاوة), unlike دْ.
ئْ: the sound is cut off completely (الشدة); the سَ after it lets it run (الرخاوة).
لْ: not cut off, not free; part of the sound runs (التوسط, «لِنْ عُمَرْ»).
نْ before خ, shown clearly: part of the sound runs; that is التوسط.
بْ: the lips close and the sound is fully held (الشدة), then released with قلقلة.

definition: الاستعلاء: the back of the tongue rises toward the palate, so the letter is always heavy. Its 7 letters gather in «خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ». Its opposite is الاستفال. الإطباق: the tongue also covers the palate, in ص ض ط ظ, the heaviest letters. Its opposite is الانفتاح.
letters: الاستعلاء: خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ · الإطباق: ص ض ط ظ
list: Six letters are said lightly from the tip of the tongue or the lips: «فِرَّ مِن لُّبٍّ» (الإذلاق). The rest are مصمتة.

facts.q: Which phrase gathers the letters of الاستعلاء?
facts.why: These 7 letters are always heavy.

facts.q: Which are the letters of الإطباق?
facts.why: The tongue covers the palate on these four.

facts.q: Every مطبق letter is also…
facts.why: The four مطبق letters are among the seven مستعلي letters.

facts.q: What is الاستعلاء?
options: The back of the tongue rises
The tongue lies low in the mouth
facts.why: Toward the palate, so the letter is heavy. Its opposite, الاستفال, keeps the tongue low and the letter light.

facts.q: Which letter is مستفل (light)?
facts.why: س is not in خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ.

facts.q: Which phrase gathers the letters of الإذلاق?
facts.why: ف ر م ن ل ب.

facts.q: Which group has the strongest heaviness?
facts.why: الإطباق adds to الاستعلاء.

طّ: rising and covering together, a full, heavy sound.

definition: الصفير: a whistle-like sound in ص ز س. القلقلة: a bounce when ق ط ب ج د («قُطْبُ جَدٍ») have a سكون. اللين: وْ and يْ after a فتحة are said softly and easily, as in خَوْفٍ and بَيْتِ.

facts.q: Which letters have الصفير?
facts.why: Their narrow gap makes the whistle.

facts.q: Which phrase gathers the letters of القلقلة?
facts.why: ق ط ب ج د.

facts.q: When does القلقلة sound?
options: When the letter has a سكون
Only when it has a شدة
facts.why: In the middle of a word or at a stop. A voweled قلقلة letter does not bounce.

facts.q: What are the letters of اللين?
options: وْ and يْ after a فتحة
و and ي after ضمة and كسرة
facts.why: As in خَوْفٍ and بَيْتِ.

facts.q: Which word has a لين letter?
facts.why: The يْ after a فتحة in قُرَيْشٍ is لين; the others are حروف مد.

facts.q: Why do the قلقلة letters bounce?
facts.why: With a سكون neither sound nor breath flows until the bounce. The bounce lets a fully closed letter be heard.

facts.q: Which of these has صفير?
facts.why: ز is one of ص ز س.

بْ is a قلقلة letter: with سكون it bounces lightly, here mid-reading.
وْ after a فتحة is a لين letter: said softly and easily, with no madd here.
زْ: a whistle like ص and س, from the same place.
دْ: a قلقلة letter; it bounces with its سكون before زَ.

جْ: a قلقلة letter bouncing inside the word.

definition: الانحراف: the sound leans, after leaving its مخرج, toward another (ل ر). التكرير: the ر tends to trill; you learn it in order to avoid it. التفشي: the air spreads in the mouth with ش. الاستطالة: the sound of ض runs along the edge of the tongue until it nears the place of ل.

facts.q: Which letters have الانحراف?
facts.why: Their sound leans toward another مخرج.

facts.q: What should you do with التكرير of the ر?
facts.why: So the ر is not rolled. التكرير is learned in order to avoid overdoing it, especially on a رّ.

facts.q: التفشي belongs to…
facts.why: The air spreads through the mouth with ش.

facts.q: الاستطالة belongs to…
facts.why: The sound of ض stretches along the edge of the tongue.

facts.q: Which letter has التكرير?
facts.why: Only ر.

facts.q: In خَرَّ (ر with شدة), what is the main risk?
facts.why: A ر with شدة is where the trill slips in most.

facts.q: What is الانحراف?
options: The sound bounces at the end
The sound leans to another مخرج
facts.why: In ل and ر.

definition: Merge the نون الساكنة or تنوين into the next letter and hold a غنة of two counts. The letters gather in يَنْمُو.
letters: ي ن م و
conditions: Only across two words: the نون ends one word and the letter starts the next.

With ن and م the merge is complete (إدغام كامل). With ي and و it is incomplete (إدغام ناقص): the غنة of the نون stays.
حفص من طريق الشاطبية reads يسٓ ۝ وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ and نٓ ۚ وَٱلْقَلَمِ with إظهار, when you join them.
tip: Hold the غنة for its two counts; don't clip it, and don't let it turn into a full ن.

مَن runs into يَخْشَىٰ: no full ن is heard, but its two-count غنة stays.

contrast.note: Before خ the ن of لِمَنْ stays clear: no merging, no held غنة.

examples.note: The ن of مِّن merges into the م of مَّسَدٍۭ.
The ن of مِن merges into the و of وَالٍ, keeping its غنة.

conditions: حفص من طريق الشاطبية: 4 (التوسط, read first) or 5 (فويق التوسط). Six counts while joining is from طريق الطيبة.
tip: Use the same length every time. In this route المتصل and المنفصل are read equal: 4 with 4, or 5 with 5.

examples.note: The ا before the همزة in the same word is held four or five counts.
The و of سُوٓءَ before the همزة: four or five counts.
The ي of سِىٓءَ before the همزة: four or five counts.
وَرَآءَ: hold the ا four or five counts before the همزة.
عَطَآءً: the same length before the همزة.
حُنَفَآءَ: keep the length equal to the others.
In شَآءَ a همزة follows the ا in the same word: hold it four or five counts.

contrast.note: In وَشَاهِدٍ no همزة follows the ا: two counts only.

examples.note: The ي before the همزة in وَجِا۟ىٓءَ: four or five counts. The small-circled ا is not read.

en: Permitted, hamza in the next word
definition: A حرف مد ends a word and the next word starts with a همزة.
conditions: حفص من طريق الشاطبية: 4 (التوسط, read first) or 5 counts. Shortening it to 2 is from طريق الطيبة, not this route.
Only when you join the two words. If you stop on the first word it is a مد طبيعي.
tip: Choose one length and keep it through your whole recitation, equal to your المتصل: 4 with 4, or 5 with 5.

examples.note: The ا at the end of لَآ is held four or five counts before أَعْبُدُ.
The ي of فِىٓ is held long before the همزة of أَحْسَنِ.
The و of قَالُوٓا۟ is held long before إِنَّ; the ا after it is not read.
مَآ أَغْنَىٰ: the ا held four or five counts.
يَدَآ أَبِى: the same length as your other منفصل.
فِىٓ أَىِّ: the ي held long before the همزة.
The همزة is in the next word: the ا of وَمَآ is held long only when you join.

contrast.note: In مَآءَهَا the همزة is in the same word: متصل, held long whether you join or not.

examples.note: The و of يَلْبَثُوٓا۟ held long before إِلَّا; the ا after the و is silent.
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا: يَا and أَيُّهَا are written joined but are two words, so this is منفصل.

definition: A صلة (the pronoun هـ between two voweled letters) where the next word starts with a همزة. It is read like المنفصل.

counts.note: 4 or 5 counts, the same as your المنفصل

conditions: Only when stopping. If you keep reading it is a normal two-count مد.

definition: وْ or يْ after a فتحة (حرفا اللين), when you stop on the letter after it.
conditions: When you keep reading, a لين letter is not lengthened at all.
tip: When اللين and العارض both come in one recitation, اللين may not be longer than العارض. If العارض is 2, اللين is 2; if العارض is 4, اللين is 2 or 4; if العارض is 6, اللين is 2, 4 or 6.

Stopping: خَوْفْ. The وْ after a فتحة, 2, 4 or 6.
Stopping: ٱلْبَيْتْ. Soft يْ, 2, 4 or 6.
Stopping: عَيْنَيْنْ. Stretch only the last يْ.
Stopping: ٱلنَّجْدَيْنْ. Soft يْ before the stopped ن.

Stopping: وَٱلصَّيْفْ. The ي has سكون after a فتحة: a soft glide.

contrast.note: Stopping: ٱلْفِيلْ. The ي after a كسرة is a true مد, العارض.

Carry on from the next word

examples.note: ۘ (م) الوقف اللازم: stop on قَوْلُهُمْ; joining would make إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ sound like their words.

ۖ (صلى) الوصل أولى: you may stop on أَذِلَّةً, but joining is better.
ۗ (قلى) الوقف أولى: you may join, but stopping on جَآءَنِى is better.
∴ ∴ تعانق الوقف: stop on لَا رَيْبَ or on فِيهِ, never on both.

ۗ (قلى): stopping on خَلَقَهَا is better.

en: How to stop on a word
definition: Stopping changes the last letter of the word.
list: التاء المربوطة becomes a هاء ساكنة
A ت written open (رَحْمَتَ، نِعْمَتَ) stays a ت ساكنة in حفص
الروم (part of the vowel, said quietly) and الإشمام (rounding the lips after the سكون, with no sound) are optional ways to hint at the last vowel. Learn them from a teacher.

facts.q: How do you stop on نَسْتَعِينُ?
facts.why: The last vowel becomes a سكون.

facts.q: How do you stop on عَلِيمًا?
facts.why: تنوين الفتح becomes an alif (مد العوض).

facts.q: How do you stop on رَحْمَةً?
facts.why: التاء المربوطة becomes a هاء ساكنة, even with تنوين الفتح.

facts.q: What is الروم?
options: Saying part of the last vowel quietly
Rounding the lips with no sound
facts.why: About a third of the vowel, heard only by someone close.

facts.q: How does حفص stop on رَحْمَتَ when it is written with an open ت?
facts.why: A ت written open stays a ت ساكنة; only a تاء مربوطة becomes a هاء.

facts.q: What is الإشمام at a stop?
options: Saying part of the vowel quietly
Adding a هاء after the letter
Rounding the lips, with no sound
facts.why: As for a ضمة, right after the سكون. It is seen, not heard.

facts.q: On which vowel can الإشمام be used?
facts.why: الروم works on ضمة and كسرة; الإشمام on ضمة only; neither on فتحة.

facts.q: Can الروم or الإشمام be used on a فتحة?
facts.why: Neither is used on a فتحة.

examples.note: Stopping: the ضمة on the last ل goes, and you say ٱلْمُزَّمِّلْ.
تنوين الفتح becomes a long ا at the stop: أَبَدَا (2 counts).
The تاء مربوطة becomes a هاء ساكنة at the stop: ٱلْقِيَٰمَهْ.
A كسرة at the end also becomes a سكون: كَٱلْعِهْنْ.
تنوين الضم is dropped at the stop: لَوَٰقِعْ.
ةً stops as هـ, not ا: وَٰحِدَهْ.
A فتحة at the end becomes a سكون: أُفِكْ.
تنوين الكسر is dropped too: دَافِعْ.
A فتحة at the end becomes a سكون: فَعَدَلَكْ.

definition: A very short pause, without taking a breath, then you carry on. حفص من طريق الشاطبية has it in four places, when you join the words.
list: مَالِيَهْ ۜ هَلَكَ (69:28-29): سكت (read first) or إدغام. Between الأنفال and التوبة: الوقف، السكت or الوصل, all without البسملة.
Other سكتات of حفص (on ال، شَىْء، or a ساكن before a همزة) are from طريق الطيبة.

examples.note: Required سكت on the ل, no breath, then رَانَ: the ل is not merged into the ر.
Required سكت on the ن, no breath, then رَاقٍ: the ن stays clear, not merged into the ر.
وَقِيلَ مَنْ ۜ رَاقٍ: سكت on the ن, so it stays a clear ن.

contrast.note: No سكت: the ن merges into the ر with no غنة, and the ر is doubled.

examples.note: ۜ and ۗ: joining, سكت on the ا; stopping (preferred here) is also correct.

examples.note: Two ways: الروم (الاختلاس), part of the first ن's ضمة with no merge; or merge with الإشمام. Your teacher picks the first.

definition: The second همزة is said softly, between a همزة and an alif. In حفص it is required in only one word: ءَا۬عْجَمِىٌّ (41:44).
tip: Another word with two readings in حفص: ضَعْف in سورة الروم (30:54, three times) may be read with فتحة or ضمة on the ض; فتحة is read first.
list: ءَآلذَّكَرَيْنِ (6:143، 6:144)، ءَآلْـَٔانَ (10:51، 10:91)، ءَآللَّهُ (10:59، 27:59): the first way is الإبدال (a long alif of 6 counts); التسهيل is also correct.

examples.note: Required: the second همزة is eased, between a همزة and an ا, short, with no مد.
ءَا۬عْجَمِىٌّ وَعَرَبِىٌّ: the second همزة is eased, with no مد after it.

contrast.note: ءَايَٰتُهُۥٓ: a full همزة, then a real ا (مد البدل, 2 counts). Stopped here, so no صلة.

examples.note: Two ways: الإبدال, an ا of 6 counts (read first, and what the reciter reads), or التسهيل with no مد.
ءَآلْـَٰٔنَ: الإبدال with 6 counts (first) or التسهيل with no مد.
ءَآللَّهُ: الإبدال with 6 counts (first) or التسهيل with no مد.
ءَآللَّهُ again: the same two ways, الإبدال first.

definition: Every letter carries a mark that tells you how to say it: a short vowel (فتحة َ، ضمة ُ، كسرة ِ), no vowel (سكون ْ), a doubled letter (شدة ّ) or a final ن sound (تنوين ً ٌ ٍ). Lengths in tajweed are counted in حركات: one حركة is the time of one short vowel.
list: the letter with no vowel, closed: قُلْ
the letter twice, the first with سكون: رَبِّ = رَبْ + بِ
a ن with سكون said (not written) at the end of a noun: أَحَدٌ = أَحَدُنْ
ا after فتحة، و after ضمة، ي after كسرة: held 2 حركات (مَٰلِكِ، يَقُولُ، ٱلرَّحِيمِ)
tip: Count a حركة by closing or opening one finger at your normal reading speed. Keep the same speed for every count in one recitation.

examples.note: فتحة on the م: an open a, one short count.
سكون on the ل: the letter is closed, with no vowel after it.
شدة: the ب is said twice, the first with سكون: رَبْ + بِ.
ضمة on the ي: a rounded u, lips forward.
كسرة on the ه: an i, lips spread.
تنوين: a ن is heard after the ضمة, نَارُنْ, because the reading goes on to حَامِيَةٌ.

facts.q: What does a سكون (ْ) on a letter mean?
options: Say it twice, the first time quietly
Do not say it at all
facts.why: The letter is said closed, with no vowel after it.

facts.q: What does a شدة (ّ) mean?
options: The letter is said twice, the first with سكون
The letter is silent and only written
The letter is heavy, with a full mouth
The letter is lengthened by two counts
facts.why: رَبِّ is رَبْ + بِ.

facts.q: What is the تنوين in أَحَدٌ?
options: A long u held for four counts
A ن with سكون said at the end
A short stop before the next word
facts.why: تنوين is a ن sound that is said but not written.

facts.q: How long is one حركة?
options: Exactly one second, by the clock
As long as it takes to say a whole ayah
The time of one short vowel
Two beats of a fast heartbeat
facts.why: Lengths in tajweed are counted in حركات; the speed follows your reading speed.

facts.q: How long is the ا in مَٰلِكِ (a natural مد)?
facts.why: A حرف مد with no همزة or سكون after it is 2 حركات.

facts.q: Which letter is a حرف مد in يَقُولُ?
options: ي at the start of the word
ل with its ضمة at the end
facts.why: و with سكون after a ضمة is a حرف مد.

definition: Before you recite, say the استعاذة (أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ). At the start of every surah except التوبة (براءة), say the بسملة too. Between them and the surah you may stop or join, in four ways.
list: At the start of a surah: 4 ways, all allowed
Stop after each (قطع الجميع) · join all three (وصل الجميع) · stop after the استعاذة, join the بسملة to the surah · join the استعاذة to the بسملة, stop, then the surah
Stop after each · join all · stop at the surah's end, then join the بسملة to the next surah
Between two surahs: 1 way not allowed
Joining the end of a surah to the بسملة and then stopping: it sounds as if the بسملة belonged to the surah before
No بسملة: stop, pause (سكت), or join
Starting in the middle of a surah
استعاذة, and the بسملة is your choice
tip: Learn one way first, usually stopping after each part (قطع الجميع), and use it every time until it is natural.

examples.text: فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ
examples.note: The command to seek refuge before reciting. The words you say (أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ…) are not themselves an ayah.
التوبة opens with no بسملة: start it with the استعاذة only.
The command word itself: fa-staʿidh, «seek refuge». The ٱ is not said.
The بسملة, said at the start of every surah except التوبة: the words you will say most.

facts.q: What is the usual wording of the استعاذة?
facts.why: It follows 16:98 «فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ».

facts.q: How many ways are allowed to start a surah with the استعاذة and the بسملة?
facts.why: Stop after each, join all, or join one pair and stop at the other.

facts.q: Between two surahs, which way is NOT allowed?
options: Stop after the surah, after the بسملة, then start
Join the surah's end to the بسملة, then stop
Stop after the surah, then join the بسملة to the next
facts.why: It makes the بسملة sound like part of the surah before.

facts.q: Which surah does not start with the بسملة?
facts.why: التوبة (براءة) is written with no بسملة, and none is read at its start.

facts.q: You start reading in the middle of a surah. The بسملة is…
facts.why: The استعاذة is said; the بسملة may be said or left.

facts.q: Going straight from الأنفال into التوبة, what can you do?
options: Say the بسملة, as at every surah start
Stop, pause (سكت) or join, no بسملة
Only stop, then say the بسملة
facts.why: All three are read for حفص; the بسملة is never said there.

facts.q: Where is the بسملة part of an ayah in the middle of a surah?
facts.why: «إِنَّهُۥ مِن سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَإِنَّهُۥ بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ».

review.notes: The four ways and the three-plus-one between surahs are agreed. Whether the استعاذة is سنة (most scholars) or واجب, and whether to say it aloud or quietly, depend on the setting (alone, in a class, in prayer); the teacher should say which to use. Some teachers also allow other wordings of the استعاذة. Starting in the middle of براءة: الميزان reports one view forbidding the بسملة and one allowing it.

definition: Seven letters are always heavy (مفخم): خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ, gathered in «خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ». The back of the tongue rises, the mouth fills and the sound is full. All other letters are light (مرقق), except ر and the ل of اللَّه, which change by rule, and the ا, which follows the letter before it.
letters: خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ
list: 1 · with فتحة and an ا after it (strongest)
The ا follows the letter before it
heavy in قَا، light in مَا
heavy with فتحة or ضمة (رَبِّ), light with كسرة (رِجَالٌ); the full ر rules come later
The غنة of الإخفاء and الإقلاب
follows the letter after it: heavy before ص ض ط ظ ق (مَن طَغَىٰ، يَنقَلِبُ), light before the others
tip: Keep the vowel true: a heavy letter with كسرة is still an i (قِ), not a heavy e; and do not let the heaviness spill onto the light letter next to it (ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ: only the ق is heavy).

examples.note: خ with a فتحة: the back of the tongue rises and the sound is full.
ق with a فتحة and an ا after it: the strongest level; the ا is heavy too.
ق with a كسرة: the weakest level, still heavy. Only the ق; the letters around it stay light.
غ with a plain فتحة, no ا after it (level 2): heavy and full.
ط with a فتحة: ط is the strongest of the heavy letters.
ص with a سكون: level 4, heavy and steady.
ص with a ضمة (level 3): the tongue rises, the sound is full and deep.

contrast.note: س with a ضمة: the same place as ص, but light; the tongue stays low.

examples.note: ر with a فتحة: heavy (the basic rule; the full ر rules come later).
The hidden ن before ط: its غنة is heavy, following the ط.

facts.q: Which letters are always heavy?
options: خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ
facts.why: حروف الاستعلاء, gathered in «خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ».

facts.q: Which is the heaviest form of a heavy letter?
facts.why: قَا in ٱلْقَارِعَةُ: فتحة, then an ا that follows it.

facts.q: Is the ق in ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ heavy?
options: No, the كسرة makes it light
facts.why: A heavy letter stays heavy with كسرة; it is the weakest level.

facts.q: How is the ا in قَالَ said?
options: Light, like every ا in the Quran
With a غنة from the nose
Short, with no length at all
facts.why: The ا has no weight of its own; it follows the letter before it.

facts.q: How is the ا in مَالِكِ said?
options: Heavy, like every ا in the Quran
With a كسرة, like the ل
facts.why: It follows the light م.

facts.q: Which four letters are the strongest heavy letters (الإطباق)?
facts.why: With these the tongue presses up against the palate.

facts.q: ر with فتحة, as in رَبِّ, is…
facts.why: ر is heavy with فتحة or ضمة and light with كسرة. The full ر rules come in a later lesson.

review.notes: The seven letters and "the ا follows the letter before it" are agreed. The levels differ: some books count five (as here, after ابن الجزري and المتولي), others three (by vowel only, سكون taking the vowel before it). Which scheme to drill is for the teacher.

definition: Two letters with سكون cannot be said one after the other. This lesson is about two words joined: the first ends in a ساكن (a حرف مد, another ساكن letter, ميم الجمع or a تنوين) and the second starts with همزة الوصل, which is not said when joined, so a ساكن meets the first. A حرف مد then drops in speech; any other ساكن takes a vowel.
list: The first is a حرف مد: it drops in speech
فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ → فِلْعُقَدِ · وَقَالَا ٱلْحَمْدُ → وَقَالَلْحَمْدُ
The first is another ساكن: usually كسرة
تنوين: its ن takes a كسرة
At a stop, two sukuns are allowed
tip: The مد letter is still written, so the eye wants to lengthen it. In فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ say a short فِ straight into the ل.

examples.note: Joined, the ى of فِى is not said: فِ runs into the ل (فِلْعُقَدِ).
بَلْ meets the ساكن ل of ٱلَّذِينَ, so its ل takes a كسرة: بَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ.
Joined, the و of ذُو is not said: ذُلْعَرْشِ.
Joined, the ا of وَإِذَا is not said: وَإِذَلْجِبَالُ.
ميم الجمع takes a ضمة before ال: هُمُ ٱلْكَفَرَةُ.
مِنْ takes a فتحة before ال: مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ.
Joined, the ى of فِى drops: فِ goes straight into the صّ (فِصُّورِ).

contrast.note: Before دِينِ (no ساكن) the ي of فِى keeps its two counts.

examples.note: The تنوين of نُوحٌ takes a كسرة before the ساكن ب: نُوحُنِ ٱبْنَهُ.

facts.q: How do you read فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ joined?
facts.why: The حرف مد drops in speech because a ساكن follows.

facts.q: Why does قُلْ become قُلِ in قُلِ ٱللَّهُمَّ?
options: To show respect for the name اللَّه
It is a different word with a كسرة
Because of the شدة on the ل after it
facts.why: كسرة is the default vowel for removing التقاء الساكنين.

facts.q: Which vowel does ميم الجمع take before ال (هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ)?
facts.why: It goes back to its original ضمة.

facts.q: Which vowel does مِنْ take before ال?
facts.why: مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ: فتحة, for lightness.

facts.q: Is the ا of وَقَالَا said in وَقَالَا ٱلْحَمْدُ?
options: Yes, four counts before the ل
facts.why: It is said only when you stop on وَقَالَا.

facts.q: Two sukuns meet at a stop, as in نَسْتَعِينْ. Is that allowed?
options: No, a vowel must be added
Only in the reading of حفص
Only when a شدة comes before it
facts.why: At a stop the meeting is allowed; the حرف مد before it becomes المد العارض.

sources.title: الميزان في أحكام تجويد القرآن (فريال زمزمي)، التقاء الساكنين
غاية المريد في علم التجويد (عطية قابل نصر)، التقاء الساكنين

review.notes: Rules for dropping the حرف مد and the vowel given to a ساكن are agreed (grammar and tajweed books).

definition: Some letters in the muṣḥaf are part of the spelling but are not said. A small round zero (۟) on a letter means it is never said. A small upright oval (۠) on an alif means it is said only when you stop on that word.
list: ءَامَنُوا۟ (the ا after واو الجماعة) · أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ (the و) · مِا۟ئَةَ (the ا) · لَأَا۟ذْبَحَنَّهُۥ · بِأَيْي۟دٍ
أَنَا۠ · لَّٰكِنَّا۠ (18:38) · ٱلظُّنُونَا۠ · ٱلرَّسُولَا۠ · ٱلسَّبِيلَا۠ (الأحزاب) · قَوَارِيرَا۠ (76:15)
Joined: no ا. At a stop: سَلَٰسِلَا or سَلَٰسِلْ, both from حفص
Never with ا, joined or stopping (قَوَارِيرْ)
tip: أَنَا before a همزة (أَنَا۠ أُحْىِۦ) stays short when joined: the ا is not said, so there is no مد منفصل.

examples.note: The ا after واو الجماعة is written, not said: the word ends on the و.
The و is not said: read أُلَٰٓئِكَ.
Joined to عَابِدٌ, the ا of أَنَا۠ is not said: أَنَ.
The ا after the و is not said: يَتْلُو.
The ا is not said: مِئَةَ.
The second ي is not said: بِأَيْدٍ.
Joined: أَنَ أُحْيِي. No ا is said, so no مد before the همزة.

contrast.note: إِنَّآ before أَعْطَيْنَٰكَ: the ا is said and held 4 or 5 counts.

examples.note: At the ayah's end you stop, so the ا is said: ٱلظُّنُونَا.
The ا is never said: joined قَوَارِيرَ مِن, stopping قَوَارِيرْ.
The ا after the همزة is not said: لَأَذْبَحَنَّهُۥ.

facts.q: What does the small round zero (۟) on a letter mean?
options: Say it at a stop only
facts.why: It marks a letter that is written but never said.

facts.q: What does the small upright oval (۠) on an alif mean?
options: Said when joined only, not at a stop
facts.why: أَنَا۠ is أَنَ when joined and أَنَا at a stop.

facts.q: How is أَنَا۠ عَابِدٌ read when joined?
facts.why: The ا of أَنَا is said only at a stop.

facts.q: Is the ا after واو الجماعة (ءَامَنُوا۟) said?
facts.why: It is a spelling convention; the word ends in the و.

facts.q: How does حفص stop on سَلَٰسِلَا۟ (76:4)?
options: Only with the ا, as written
With the ا or without it
It may not be stopped on at all
facts.why: Both ways are read from حفص; joined, there is no ا.

facts.q: How is أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ read?
options: أُو لَٰٓئِكَ, with a long و
facts.why: The و is written but not said.

غاية المريد في علم التجويد (عطية قابل نصر)، الحروف التي تحذف وصلًا
مصحف المدينة (نص Tanzil)، علامتا ۟ و۠
sources.locator: علامات الضبط في الخاتمة؛ الكلمات في الأمثلة

review.notes: Read against the marks of مصحف المدينة (Tanzil text) and the sources. سَلَٰسِلَا at a stop: both ways from حفص; العميد rates dropping the ا as stronger, the teacher may prefer one. The ا after واو الجماعة and لَأَا۟ذْبَحَنَّهُۥ rest on the muṣḥaf marks (no tajweed book passage found).

en: When two causes of مد meet
definition: Sometimes one حرف مد has two reasons to be long, for example a همزة before it (بدل) and a سكون after it (لازم). Then the stronger cause wins and the weaker one is dropped. From strongest to weakest: لازم، متصل، عارض، منفصل، بدل.
list: وَجَآءُوٓ أَبَاهُمْ: 4 or 5 joined (2 if you stop on وَجَآءُو)
tip: Ask what comes after the حرف مد first (a سكون or a همزة); the همزة before it (بدل) only decides the length when nothing comes after.

examples.note: The ا has a همزة before it and after it: المتصل wins, 4 or 5.
Stopping: the و after the همزة is بدل and عارض; العارض wins: 2, 4 or 6.
بدل and منفصل: joined, the منفصل wins, 4 or 5.
Stopping: ٱلْمَآبْ. The ا after the همزة becomes عارض: 2, 4 or 6.
رَءَآ before أَيْدِيَهُمْ: the منفصل wins, 4 or 5.
بُرَءَٰٓؤُا۟: المتصل wins, 4 or 5.
ءَآمِّينَ: بدل and a شدة after it: لازم wins, six.

contrast.note: ءَامِنِينَ: no شدة after the ا, so only the بدل: two counts.

examples.note: Stopping: مُسْتَهْزِءُونْ. بدل and عارض: 2, 4 or 6.

facts.q: Which مد is the strongest?
facts.why: Order: لازم، متصل، عارض، منفصل، بدل.

facts.q: Which مد is the weakest?
facts.why: البدل is 2 counts in حفص and gives way to any other cause.

facts.q: وَلَآ ءَآمِّينَ: the ا after the همزة is long by…
facts.why: A همزة before it (بدل) and a شدة after it (لازم): the لازم wins.

facts.q: You stop on مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ. The و is…
facts.why: The stop gives a سكون after it, so العارض wins over البدل.

facts.q: Order the causes from strongest:
facts.why: لازم › متصل › عارض › منفصل › بدل.

facts.q: رِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ: the ا is…
facts.why: A همزة after it in the same word: المتصل wins over البدل.

sources.title: غاية المريد في علم التجويد (عطية قابل نصر)، أقوى المدود وقاعدة السببين
هداية القاري إلى تجويد كلام الباري (المرصفي)، اجتماع سببين
النشر في القراءات العشر (ابن الجزري)، العمل بأقوى السببين

review.notes: The order and the rule are in the sources. With بدل + عارض some teachers limit the stop to the lengths they use for العارض elsewhere (التسوية); keep one length. ءَآلذَّكَرَيْنِ (6:143) and ءَآلْـَٔـٰنَ are مد الفرق (همزة الوصل after the question همزة, 6 or تسهيل), not بدل + لازم, so they are not used here.

definition: ض comes from the side of the tongue against the upper back teeth, and its sound stretches along the side of the tongue (الاستطالة). ظ comes from the tip of the tongue against the edges of the upper front teeth, with the tongue tip showing a little. Both are heavy, both are مطبقة; the place of the sound is what tells them apart.
letters: ض ظ
list: side of the tongue (one side or both) against the upper molars; the sound stretches from the back to the front of the side (استطالة)
tip of the tongue against the edges of the upper front teeth (like ذ and ث, but heavy)
ض said as ظ, mixed with ذ, as a heavy ل, or with a hint of ز
keep both clear: أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ، يَعَضُّ ٱلظَّالِمُ
tip: For ظ, let the tongue tip touch the upper teeth; for ض keep the tip back and press the side of the tongue, and let the sound run along it.

examples.note: ض runs along the side of the tongue; then ظ at the tip, at the teeth.
نَاضِرَةٌ (radiant): ض, from the side of the tongue.
نَاظِرَةٌ (looking): ظ, with the tongue tip at the teeth.
وَوَضَعْنَا: ض with فتحة from the side of the tongue; don't turn it into ظ.
ض with سكون: hold it on the side of the tongue.
ظ with شدة: the tongue tip stays at the teeth.
نَضْرَةَ: ض, heavy, and its sound runs along the side of the tongue.

contrast.note: نَصْرُ: ص, heavy too, but a whistle from the tongue tip.

examples.note: ض then ظ: keep both apart (الجزرية).
بِضَنِينٍ is read with ض in حفص.
ض with سكون before ط: say the ض fully, don't merge.

facts.q: Where is ض made?
options: Tip of the tongue and the upper front teeth
Side of the tongue and upper molars
Deep in the throat, near the chest
facts.why: The side (حافة) of the tongue against the upper back teeth.

facts.q: Where is ظ made?
options: Side of the tongue and the upper molars
Tongue tip and upper front teeth
Back of the tongue and the soft palate
Middle of the tongue and the hard palate
facts.why: With ذ and ث, from the tip of the tongue and the edges of the upper front teeth.

facts.q: Which quality belongs only to ض?
facts.why: The sound stretches along the side of the tongue.

facts.q: Which is a mistake Ibn al-Jazari warns against?
options: Saying ظ with the tongue tip
facts.why: In النشر he lists ض said as ظ, mixed with ذ, or as a heavy ل.

facts.q: In أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ, the ض and ظ…
options: Both become ظ, the easier letter
Both become ض, the first letter
facts.why: Ibn al-Jazari: «وَإِنْ تَلَاقَيَا: البَيَانُ لَازِمُ».

facts.q: Both ض and ظ are…
options: Light letters with a thin sound
facts.why: Both are from خص ضغط قظ and from the four مطبقة letters.

sources.title: المقدمة الجزرية (ابن الجزري، ت. عبد المحسن القاسم)، مخرج الضاد والظاء، الاستطالة، كلمات الظاء
غاية المريد في علم التجويد (عطية قابل نصر)، الفرق بين الضاد والظاء
النشر في القراءات العشر (ابن الجزري)، أخطاء الضاد

review.notes: The places of articulation are agreed. The exact sound of ض is a known modern disagreement (the common sound vs. a sound close to ظ argued from old descriptions); learn it from the teacher by ear.

en: Hinting the last vowel at a stop
definition: When you stop, the last letter usually gets a plain سكون. Two optional ways let the listener know its vowel: الروم, saying about a third of the vowel quietly, and الإشمام, rounding the lips right after the سكون with no sound.
list: سكون, روم or إشمام: نَسْتَعِينُ، أَحَدٌ
تاء مربوطة stopped as هاء (ٱلْحُطَمَةُ → ٱلْحُطَمَهْ), ميم الجمع (عَلَيْهِمْ), a vowel added only to join (قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ → قُمْ)
after ضمة/و or كسرة/ي many leave الروم and الإشمام (فِيهِ، أَمْرُهُۥ); others allow them
tip: With الروم the letter is not fully stopped: a مد عارض before it is read 2 counts only (ٱلرَّحِيمِ), while a متصل stays 4 or 5 (ٱلسَّمَآءِ) and a لازم 6. A قلقلة letter does not bounce.

examples.note: تنوين ضم: سكون, روم or إشمام. With الروم the د does not bounce (no قلقلة).
ضمة: سكون, روم or إشمام.
كسرة: سكون or روم; never إشمام.
تنوين كسر: سكون or روم.
كسرة after a مد: with الروم, the مد before it is 2 counts only.
تنوين ضم: سكون, روم or إشمام.

facts.q: What is الروم?
options: Rounding the lips after the سكون, with no sound
A third of the vowel, quietly
Lengthening the last vowel to two counts
Adding a soft هاء after the last letter
facts.why: It is heard by someone near you.

facts.q: What is الإشمام?
options: Rounding the lips, with no sound
Saying the full vowel, but quietly
A nasal sound from the nose
A quiet فتحة on the last letter
facts.why: It is seen, not heard.

facts.q: Which vowels take الروم?
facts.why: Not فتحة.

facts.q: Which vowel takes الإشمام?
facts.why: Rounding the lips shows a ضمة only.

facts.q: Stopping on ٱلْحُطَمَةُ, can you use الروم?
options: No: it becomes a هاء ساكنة
facts.why: The stopped هاء has no vowel to hint at.

facts.q: Stopping on قُمِ (قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ), can you use الروم?
options: No: that كسرة is only for joining
It is required at every stop
facts.why: A vowel added for التقاء الساكنين is not hinted at.

facts.q: With الروم on ٱلرَّحِيمِ, the مد عارض before the last letter is…
options: 6 counts, as in a full stop
Dropped, the مد is not said
facts.why: الروم is like joining, so only the short way (2) of المد العارض is read. A متصل (ٱلسَّمَآءِ) stays 4 or 5 and a لازم 6 (هداية القاري، الوافي).

sources.title: المقدمة الجزرية (ابن الجزري، ت. عبد المحسن القاسم)، الوقف بالروم والإشمام
متن الشاطبية (حرز الأماني)، باب الوقف على أواخر الكلم
الوافي في شرح الشاطبية (القاضي)، الروم والإشمام وهاء الضمير
الميزان في أحكام تجويد القرآن (فريال زمزمي)، الروم والإشمام

review.notes: Allowed and forbidden cases are agreed. The amount of الروم and the lip shape of الإشمام are performance, learnt by ear and sight from a teacher. هاء الضمير: the Shatibiyya reports both views; ask which the teacher follows. With الروم only المد العارض shortens to 2; a متصل stays 4–5 and a لازم 6 (هداية القاري 22869; الوافي 38075/173–177).

definition: The Quran may be read at three speeds, all with every rule kept: التحقيق (slow, for learning and teaching), التدوير (medium) and الحدر (quick). الترتيل is the quality of a careful, measured reading; many count it as a speed close to التحقيق, others as the manner that covers all three.
list: slowest: every letter and length given in full; for learning and teaching
between the two: the usual speed for many readers
quick, but with no rule dropped: مد lengths, غنة and clear letters stay
calm and measured, with attention to meaning (73:4 «وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا»)
tip: Keep one choice of each مد length through a recitation, at any speed. A حركة is timed by your pace, so a count is shorter in الحدر, but the number of counts stays the same.

facts.q: Which speed is used for learning and teaching?
facts.why: The slowest reading, with every letter given in full.

facts.q: What is الحدر?
options: A quick reading that keeps every rule
A quick reading that drops the long مد
Reading silently, with the eyes only
A slow reading with long pauses
facts.why: Speed never excuses dropping a rule.

facts.q: التدوير is…
options: Only used in the night prayer
facts.why: The middle speed.

facts.q: Which ayah commands الترتيل?
facts.why: «وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا».

facts.q: In الحدر, the غنة of a نّ is…
options: Said as a ن with سكون
facts.why: The rules stay; only the speed changes.

facts.q: According to Ibn al-Jazari (النشر), is التحقيق a kind of الترتيل?
options: Only in the reading of حفص
facts.why: «كل تحقيق ترتيل وليس كل ترتيل تحقيقا».

sources.title: النشر في القراءات العشر (ابن الجزري)، التحقيق والحدر والتدوير والترتيل
الميزان في أحكام تجويد القرآن (فريال زمزمي)، مراتب القراءة
غاية المريد في علم التجويد (عطية قابل نصر)، مراتب القراءة

review.notes: All three speeds are agreed. The terms differ: الميزان gives three levels with الترتيل covering all, غاية المريد puts الترتيل as a level with التحقيق as a fourth in some views, العميد counts four. The card gives the النشر view.
